questions.q: According to this lesson's review, what is the exam-relevant lesson behind Caldwell's Problem Management work on the Line 3 printer?
options: Problem records should never be linked to more than one Incident
Problem Management is deliberately slower than Incident Management, because it's chasing a permanent cause rather than a fast workaround
Problem Management should always resolve faster than Incident Management
Problem Management replaces the need for Incident Management entirely
questions.explain: An exam question implying Problem should move at Incident's pace is testing whether you've internalized that the two processes optimize for different things.

questions.q: What exam-relevant principle does this lesson draw from Caldwell's Change Enablement work on Meridian?
options: All changes to a production system must always go through Emergency approval
Risk assessment questionnaires are optional once a system is marked business-critical
CAB review is only relevant to Standard changes
Risk should be calculated from real, checkable answers and should programmatically drive how much approval a change needs
questions.explain: A calculated risk value that nobody acts on, or one typed by hand, defeats the purpose — the exam tests whether risk is real and consequential.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a Requested Item SLA, rather than one SLA on the overall Request, is the exam-relevant takeaway from the New Hire IT Setup catalog item?
options: Because SLAs are not relevant to Request Management at all
Because sc_request records cannot technically carry any kind of state field
Because every catalog item in an order always shares the exact same fulfillment timeline
Because a multi-item order fulfills item by item, and the Request's own status should be a calculated rollup rather than an independently set field
questions.explain: Item-level SLAs and a rolled-up Request status reflect how real, multi-item fulfillment actually works — a point the exam tests directly.

questions.q: Where did a `cmdb_ci` reference do real work earlier in this capstone, without the course explaining what a CMDB actually is?
options: Only in the SLA Definitions built in Lesson 31
Nowhere — this course never referenced `cmdb_ci` at any point
In Lesson 30's `root_cause` field on the Problem record, and in the Change Risk Assessment question about touching a business-critical Configuration Item
Only in the Service Portal widget built in Lesson 31
questions.explain: Both references used Configuration Item data to do real work (identifying a root cause, scoring change risk) without the course ever explaining the CMDB underneath them.

questions.q: What does this lesson say Course 9 picks up, based on the gap this course deliberately left open?
options: A second Service Portal widget for the same New Hire catalog item
A deeper dive into Incident Management's Priority Lookup Rule
What a CMDB actually is, how a CI relationship is modeled, and how Discovery populates that data automatically
A replacement for the Change Enablement risk questionnaire built in this course
questions.explain: Course 9, ServiceNow CMDB, CSDM & Discovery, is positioned specifically to explain the CI and CMDB concepts this course used but never taught.
